assistant:
## Warning and prevention

The undervoltage episode lasted **18:45–20:45** on 6 January, with Bus_29 reaching a low of **0.932 p.u. at 19:15**. A warning was visible at **18:30**, when the voltage was **0.952 p.u.**—**15 minutes** before the episode began.

The single action tested—raising Gen_bus7’s voltage set-point from **1.000 to 1.014 p.u.**—did **not** prevent the episode when held throughout it: Bus_29 still fell to **0.940 p.u.**, and line **Bus_5 → Bus_7 [L9]** became overloaded.

A separate coordinated active-power redispatch plan passed the power-flow checks at all **10 sampled moments** from 18:30 to 20:45. It kept the minimum voltage at **0.950 p.u.** and maximum loading at **90.0%**, assuming a modeled ramp limit of **20% of capacity per hour**. This shows a feasible steady-state plan in the model; it does **not** establish that the actual units could deliver it on time, because their actual ramp capabilities were not checked.

**Scope note:** The cause diagnosis is for **20:00**; the prevention plan covers **18:30–20:45**. Those figures describe different study scopes and should be read separately.

## Recurrence and cause

Bus_29 undervoltage recurred **12 times** in the measurements week. Of the **10 episodes investigated**, demand was the main cause in each, accounting for **70.6–71.6%** of the voltage change. At 20:00, nearby demand rose from **12.95 to 14.12 MW** and explained **71.1%** of the drop; demand elsewhere contributed **28.7%**. The measured generator-output change was ruled out as a material cause.

## Not established by these studies

The results are steady-state power-flow analyses. They do not establish whether Bus_29 was near voltage collapse, whether real unit ramp rates would allow the plan, or how dynamic behavior would affect the event. Establishing those would require, respectively, a voltage-stability margin study, unit-specific ramp and response data with a deliverability analysis, and a time-domain dynamic study using validated models.

The grid data also do not establish *why* demand rose. Weather, calendar or scheduled activity, and specific customer behavior remain untested; aligned weather and schedule records and customer-level interval metering or activity records would be needed. The **cost attributable to the demand rise** is likewise not established; that requires a counterfactual cost study with verified price inputs.

📋 Data source: measurements. Load reactive demand was derived using the default **0.95 lagging power factor**.
